task.description: Validate src/design/iss0612-provisioning-lock-scope-fix.md, a Type E design fixing ISS-0612/GH-556's confirmed root cause: provisionTenantSchema()'s advisory-lock block (provisioning.zig:117-125) closes its own scope before Steps 2-6a (the real work) even begin, so concurrent same-tenant calls race unprotected. The design proposes: (1) restructure so a single lock_conn, acquired once, is reused across Step 2 (idempotency check), Steps 3-4 (bpm_provision_tenant_schema() call), Step 6 (timestamp update), and Step 6a (tenant promotion), with lock release + connection release as one defer pair covering every exit path; (2) Step 5 (runForSchema migrations) deliberately keeps its own separate connection rather than sharing lock_conn, with an explicit deadlock analysis concluding no cross-lock wait-for cycle exists between the tenant-level session lock and MIGRATIONS_LOCK_KEY_SQL's global xact-scoped lock (different connections, disjoint keyspaces); (3) recommends keeping bpm_provision_tenant_schema()'s internal per-schema lock as-is (protects direct SQL callers); (4) recommends adding pg_advisory_unlock_all() to Pool.release() as defense-in-depth. Verify all of this against the actual current source -- do not trust the design doc's or CODE-DESIGNER's own description without checking. This is an architecturally significant change (touches connection/transaction lifecycle in a function multiple other issues (ISS-0131, ISS-0209) already depend on) -- scrutinize the deadlock-freedom claim particularly closely, since a wrong analysis here could trade a hang for a deadlock instead of actually fixing anything.
acceptance_criteria: Design correctly restructures the lock scope to cover Steps 2-6a on a single connection
The deadlock-freedom claim between the tenant session lock and MIGRATIONS_LOCK_KEY_SQL is independently verified against actual source, not just trusted from the design doc
Design addresses the third (per-schema SQL-level) lock layer with a defensible recommendation
Design addresses the Pool.release() defense-in-depth recommendation

result.summary: Validated src/design/iss0612-provisioning-lock-scope-fix.md against the actual current source (src/db/provisioning.zig, src/db/migrations.zig, migrations/060_schema_per_tenant_bootstrap.sql, src/db/pool.zig read in full, not excerpted). All factual claims in the design check out exactly against source: (1) the current lock block at provisioning.zig:117-125 does close before Steps 2-6a begin, confirming the root cause; (2) runForSchema() (migrations.zig:104-116) has NO *Conn parameter in its signature -- it only takes *Pool and always calls pool.acquire() internally (line 112) -- so it is structurally impossible, not merely a matter of implementer discipline, for the redesigned provisionTenantSchema() to pass lock_conn into it; this is a stronger guardrail than the design claims for itself. (3) Pool.acquire() (pool.zig:779-818) only ever draws from the idle_indices/idle_count set under mutex, so a checked-out lock_conn can never be handed back out to a concurrent/nested acquire() call until release() returns it -- confirms no self-deadlock and no accidental connection reuse. (4) MIGRATIONS_LOCK_KEY_SQL (migrations.zig:31-32) is pg_advisory_xact_lock on a global (non-tenant) key, acquired on runForSchema's own connection inside its per-migration transaction (line 463) -- disjoint keyspace and disjoint connection from lock_conn's session-scoped pg_advisory_lock, so no cross-lock wait-for cycle exists; the design correctly identifies the real cost as connection-pool scarcity (two connections held per critical section pass), not a deadlock, and correctly relies on the pre-existing PoolExhausted fail-fast path. (5) bpm_provision_tenant_schema() (migrations/060_schema_per_tenant_bootstrap.sql:73-99) confirmed to take pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(v_schema_name)) at line 89 -- a third, schema-keyed, disjoint lock layer as claimed; keep-as-is recommendation is defensible since it protects direct SQL callers bypassing the Zig-side lock entirely. (6) Pool.release() (pool.zig:834-873) confirmed: resetConnectionSearchPath at line 857, mutex-guarded idle-set insertion at lines 859-873 -- the proposed pg_advisory_unlock_all() placement matches exactly. lint_design_artefact.py exits 0 (BLOCKER=0 MAJOR=0, 2 MINOR: a schema-qualified-name mention in prose describing an existing SQL function's name, and the ISS-0612 requirement-ID-format check, both expected/cosmetic for this Type E issue-fix doc). No implementation code present. Design is complete enough for BACKEND-DEV to proceed without ambiguity on connection-sharing scope.
